speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have had a fever and changes in your mental state for two days; can you describe exactly how your thinking has changed and if you have any headache or neck stiffness?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS). The combination of fever, altered mentation, and a history of haloperidol use for tics is highly suggestive of this diagnosis. I am not requesting further tests as the clinical picture is already diagnostic.
